intro: Three unconnected but useful data points today: a concrete lesson on how a real sales-research agent breaks and gets fixed in production, a hard regulatory deadline forcing EU banks to fold AI-driven cyber risk into existing resilience programs, and a core-banking platform vendor turning agent governance into a built-in feature for banks too small to build it themselves.

cards.title: Production-Ready AI Agents: 5 Lessons from Refactoring a Monolith
cards.bite: A single-script sales-research agent kept silently stalling because one failed sub-task took down the whole pipeline with no clear failure point. The fix wasn't a better model — it was breaking the monolith into narrow, independently-testable sub-agents (a Company Researcher, a Case Study Researcher, a Selector, an Email Drafter) each responsible for one job, plus circuit breakers that cap runaway token spend when something goes wrong. The lesson generalizes: agent reliability problems are usually architecture problems wearing an AI costume.
cards.read_if: Read if you sell or evaluate agent tooling and want a believable, specific failure story rather than a vendor pitch; skip if you only care about banking-specific outcomes.
cards.key_takeaway: The original agent's biggest problem wasn't the model, it was architecture: a single linear script meant one failed sub-task silently stalled the entire pipeline, and the fix was decomposing it into narrow, independently-testable sub-agents (Company Researcher, Case Study Researcher, Selector, Email Drafter) plus circuit breakers to cap runaway token spend.

cards.title: Addressing AI-enabled cybersecurity threats (Letter SSM-2026-0301 to significant institutions)
cards.bite: The ECB just sent its first letter to banks in over four years, and it's not a new AI rulebook — it's an instruction to fold AI-accelerated cyber threats into resilience programs banks already run under existing EU digital-operational-resilience rules. Every euro-area significant institution now owes its supervisory team a board-owned action plan by October 31, 2026, with a cross-bank comparison to follow. The message: frontier AI has shortened the gap between a discovered vulnerability and an actual exploit, so existing risk programs have to explicitly account for that speed.
cards.read_if: Read if you sell into EU banks and need a real date to anchor a compliance-driven conversation; skip if your book is US-only.
cards.key_takeaway: The ECB is not writing new AI rules; it is telling the ~110 banks it directly supervises that frontier AI has compressed the vulnerability-to-exploit timeline enough that DORA-mandated ICT resilience programs must now explicitly account for AI-accelerated attacks, with a board-owned action plan due by 31 October 2026 and a horizontal peer analysis to follow.

cards.title: Fiserv Launches agentOS: The Operating System for Agentic AI in Banking
cards.bite: Fiserv is packaging agent governance — identity-bound execution, policy enforcement, observability, audit trails — as built-in infrastructure rather than something each bank has to assemble, and launching it with a marketplace of Fiserv-built and third-party agents (OpenAI and AWS among the launch partners). For the thousands of mid-sized banks and credit unions running on Fiserv's core, payments, and servicing rails, this means agent governance arrives pre-installed instead of requiring a build-out. That materially changes what a smaller institution needs to buy versus what it already gets by staying on the platform.
cards.read_if: Read if you sell orchestration, governance, or observability tooling to community banks or credit unions; skip if your accounts are large banks running their own stacks.
cards.key_takeaway: agentOS bundles identity-bound execution, policy enforcement, observability and traceability as native platform primitives and ships with a marketplace of Fiserv-built and third-party agents (with OpenAI and AWS as launch collaborators), meaning banks on this stack get governance-by-design agent infrastructure rather than having to assemble it themselves.
